To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the incremental algorithm proposed in this paper is efficient, scalable, and capable of mining dynamic datasets; (2) the parallel algorithm proposed in this article is scalable and capable of mining large dynamic datasets; and (3) the asynchronous distributed algorithm proposed in this research is scalable and capable not only of mining distributed datasets, but also of generating global as well as local models of frequent itemsets, including high-contrast frequent patterns.

we present an incremental algorithm which dynamically maintains required information without examining the entire database, and we show how to parallel and distribute this algorithm for mining distributed dynamic databases, which is the first such effort in the literature.
we have developed an efficient algorithm for mining incremental data, which is capable of parallelization and can be used in a distributed environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of efficient, parallel, and distributed incremental methods for mining frequent itemsets.
the efficient implementation of data mining algorithms in the presence of dynamic, distributed, and skewed data.
the design and implementation of parallel and distributed incremental algorithms for frequent itemset mining.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed parallel and distributed approaches for incremental frequent itemsets mining are very effective and efficient.
our approach is capable of mining distributed dynamic databases efficiently.
the proposed algorithms are efficient and scalable for mining dynamic and distributed datasets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide an incremental algorithm for frequent itemset mining, which can be easily parallelized and distributed.
we present a novel algorithm for incremental frequent item mining, which is capable of efficiently mining dynamic data in a parallel and distributed environment.
we have presented a set of efficient incremental and parallel algorithms for mining frequent itemsets in dynamic and distributed environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed algorithms are scalable, and can handle very large datasets.
, by exploiting the dynamic properties of the data, it is possible to achieve significant speedups in mining dynamic datasets.

, in the case of frequent itemset generation, the incremental and distributed algorithms are not just a matter of convenience, but rather an imperative for ensuring scalability and for facilitating knowledge discovery.
